title: Synthesis fallback and hotfix coordination for siloed canary failures
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem statement: During recent mixed-mode rollouts (hosted, dedicated, private) we observed multiple tenant-scoped canary failures that did not surface in cluster-level metrics and that were exacerbated by stale KV cache state and tenant-specific quantization fallbacks. These failures produced silent quality regressions for a small set of enterprise customers, requiring manual tenant pinning and urgent hotfix builds. Goal: define a repeatable escalation + hotfix coordination lifecycle that minimizes customer impact and restores compatibility across deployment modes while preserving data residency and compliance requirements for private deployments.
background: Previous playbooks focused on broad rollback choreography but lacked a reproducible path for: 1) identifying tenant-scoped regressions that pass cluster health checks, 2) reconciling divergent KV cache states across Dedicated/Private, and 3) delivering tenant-scoped hotpatches without a full rollback. We want a synthesis approach that prefers targeted mitigation (pin, patch, edge-fallback) before global rollbacks and that clearly delineates customer communication steps and engineering responsibilities.
proposal_summary: 1) Rapid triage checklist to determine if regression is tenant-scoped or global. 2) Automated instrumentation to capture per-tenant generation diffs and model variant fingerprints (seed/config/quantization). 3) Cross-env KV cache reconciliation tools to detect stale prefixes and a safe invalidation strategy for Dedicated/Private. 4) Hotfix workflow: build -> smoke -> tenant-stage patch -> canary tether -> customer approval -> gradual rollout. 5) Communication templates and escalation ownership matrix for SE/Support/Eng.
detailed_steps: Triage (first 20m): collect request IDs, tenant ID, model variant, exact prompt, seed, and perf traces. Use /observability/tenant-diff dashboard and attach model-fingerprint from runtime headers.

Determine scope (20-45m): run tenant-sliced traffic replay in isolated sandbox to confirm reproducibility. If reproduces only for tenant slice, classify as "tenant-scoped". If reproduces across slices, escalate as "global-regression".

Mitigation ladder (45-120m): 1. Temporary model pin for affected tenant (tenant.pinned_model = previous-stable), 2. If KV-cached context suspected, run targeted cache-invalidate for tenant prefixes via ops API with a TTL bump, 3. If quantization variant suspected, route tenant to higher-precision fallback variant, 4. If none succeed, trigger full rollback per coordinated-channel protocol.

Hotfix build & verification (2-6h): branch from pinned commit, apply patch (kernel param/runner-fix/quant table), run smoke harness on sample tenant corpus, create canary tether for 5% of tenant's traffic, and monitor quality SLOs for 2 hours.

Cross-environment constraints: For Private/VPC installs, coordinate with customer infra contact and SRE to schedule patch windows and share signed binary/artifact. For Dedicated, use reserved nodes to validate before tenant reattachment.

Communication: Use templates in 'customer_comms_template' for initial acknowledgement within 30 minutes, follow-ups at 2h, and resolution summary within 24h. Provide link to status page and opt-in for artifact verification for Private deployments.

Post-incident: create postmortem with root-cause, KV cache diffs, tracing snapshots, and a regression test added to the pre-rollout harness. Schedule follow-up to automate detection of similar fingerprint changes.

If rollback needed: coordinate a time-window, pin earlier model on all affected slices, run a memory/kv reconciliation job to prevent sticky artifacts, and execute rollback in waves (tenant-first, region-first, global).
acceptance_criteria: Documented triage checklist is added to the Canary Escalation Runbook and reviewed by SRE and Applied ML.
Automated tenant-diff instrumentation emits model fingerprints and is available on the tenant-diff dashboard.
KV cache reconciliation tool can run a dry-run detect and a targeted invalidate for tenant prefixes without requiring full service restart.
Hotfix pipeline supports canary tethering and a standardized customer sign-off step for Private installs.
Customer comms templates validated by Support and Legal for private-compliance language.
customer_comms_template: Acknowledgement (within 30m): 'We are investigating a regression impacting your integration. Assigned engineer: <name>. Current mitigation: temporary pin to previous model. We'll provide an update within 2 hours. If you would like to verify artifacts for on-prem, we'll share signed build details and a verification checklist.'

2-hour update: 'Root-cause hypothesis and mitigation progress. If hotfix is ready for verification, next steps and proposed time window. Expected impact duration: <est>. Contact: se-<team>@redwood.ai.'

Resolution (24h): 'Summary of the issue, actions taken, postmortem link, and recommended follow-up (client-side prompt adjustment, if applicable). Offer a technical review session for affected customers.'
roles_and_ownership: Incident Lead: owns triage timeline and customer comms (rotation staffed by SRE/Platform Eng)
Runtime Engineer: produces hotfix, validates regression and coordinates build artifacts
Applied ML: verifies model-fingerprint diffs and checks regression against eval prompts
Support/SE: customer liaison and artifact verification for Private deployments
Release Manager: approves cross-environment rollback and orchestrates waves
security_considerations: Private deployments: do not push unsigned binaries. Provide a signed tarball and checksums; confirm transfer through customer's approved channel.
Audit: log all tenant pin/invalidate actions to audit trail and link to compliance evidence store.
Secrets: avoid including any customer PII in public comms or status updates; use internal ticket references for detailed payloads.
postmortem_actions: Add a regression test to the pre-rollout harness that covers the failing tenant prompt set.
Instrument an alert that triggers when per-tenant generation quality delta > 8% while cluster-level metrics are nominal.
Schedule a runbook review and tabletop exercise with SRE, Applied ML, and Support within 2 sprints.
Evaluate improvements to KV cache TTL heuristics and prefix eviction logic to avoid sticky stale state across rollouts.
